messages:
matt_support: heads up — multiple customers reporting p99 spikes on /v1/chat.generate starting ~09:10 UTC. spikes show longer tails (p95 -> 450ms, p99 -> 2.1s). tickets: #4521 #4522. any quick mitigation suggestions?
sara_sre: looking at infra graphs now. seeing increased queue depth on gpu-pool-3 and bursty batch sizes.
alex_dev: can you paste a sample trace id? i'll check routing + kernel selection.
matt_support: trace ids: trace-7a8b9c (customer A), trace-7a8b9d (customer B). both 99th token timeouts align with KV-cache misses.
sara_sre: KV-cache miss spike makes sense — there was a small config push to prefix-cache TTL earlier. rolling back to previous TTL now.
oncall-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-1193 — p99 spike /v1/chat.generate. Pager duty pages sent.
jana_product: customers complaining about latency regionally (eu-west). can we route eu-west traffic to dedicated-eu fallback pool?
alex_dev: suggest immediate mitigations: 1) enable circuit-breaker at route level (reject high-latency requests with 503 + Retry-After) 2) fallback routing to low-latency small-quant model (redwood-small-llm-ql8) 3) temporary tighten burst rate-limit for anonymous keys
sara_sre: i'm toggling CB now (cb-config v1.2) — if queue depth > 120 -> fast-fail. also enabling autoscale burst for dedicated-eu to accept more connections.
deploy-bot: cb-config v1.2 deployed to prod at 09:27 UTC (rollout 20% -> 100%).
matt_support: pushed a short reply to customers: "we're actively mitigating increased latency; you may see occasional 503s while we stabilize; we'll follow up with root cause."
alex_dev: routing rule applied: prefer redwood-small-llm-ql8 for requests with seq_len < 128 and customer tier != enterprise. added region override for eu-west.
sara_sre: reduced default batch size from 64 -> 32 for affected pools to reduce tail amplification.
oncall-bot: Metric alert: p99 /v1/chat.generate > 1.8s in eu-west — alert resolved at 09:42 UTC.
matt_support: are errors still happening or just latency?
jana_product: customers still seeing occasional 503s but overall p99 down to ~900ms. good but keep monitoring.
sara_sre: rolling full rollback of prefix-cache TTL patch completed at 09:35 UTC — that removed a lot of KV thrash.
alex_dev: note to ops: if p99 creeps back up, swap to cached-kv-backed model variant (redwood-medium-kv) + enable prefix prefill for gold-tier customers.
matt_support: set of quick repro steps in case we need to reproduce: 1) run ramp test hitting /v1/chat.generate with seq=64, concurrency 200, keys randomized to disable reuse; 2) monitor kv cache hit ratio and batch size histogram. attaching command snippet.
matt_support: ```bash
# repro: replays user-like traffic
wrk -t8 -c200 -d120s -s scripts/chat_ramp.lua --latency 
--vars seq_len=64 --vars model=redwood-base
```
sara_sre: warning: avoid doing full-scale repro against prod — prefer staging with traffic mirroring.
alex_dev: created canary routing: 10% to small-ql8, 90% to base for 30m test. will expand if stable.
deploy-bot: canary routing applied at 09:30 UTC (10% -> small-ql8).
jana_product: suggest follow-up for customers: offer to temporarily route them to dedicated capacity if they need stricter p99 SLA.
matt_support: noted — I'll triage impacted accounts and offer limited dedicated slots.
sara_sre: post-mortem action items: 1) add guardrail that prevents prefix-cache TTL pushes during high-qps windows 2) auto-scale headroom config tweak for gpu-pool-3 3) document quick-fallback checklist (CB, routing, batch size, small model)
alex_dev: logging improvement: include KV-cache hit ratio and batch_size in trace root to speed future triage.
oncall-bot: Follow-up tasks created: TASK-9812 (guardrail), TASK-9813 (headroom), TASK-9814 (trace-logging).
matt_support: thanks all. i'll update the affected customers and close tickets once we confirm 24h stable p99.
jana_product: adding note to release calendar: avoid cache TTL changes during big marketing demo next week. :grimacing:
sara_sre: i'll keep an eye on dashboards for next 24h. leaving this thread open until then. :eyes:
